## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O((n+m)\log\log(n+m)/\sqrt{\log(n+m)})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O((n+m)(\log\log(n+m))^2/\sqrt{\log(n+m)})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Retain declared variables. If an empty clause is present, return 0; if m = 0, return 2^n. Duplicate literals, duplicate clauses, and tautological clauses may be retained. The measures n and m refer to the original input.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n+m)$ |
| Clauses | $O(\ell+m)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. For each original clause C_j introduce an optional marker y_j. For every literal a in C_j, add the binary clause $\neg y_j\vee\neg a$, simplifying the negation of a literal in the usual way. Thus y_j can be 1 exactly when the original clause is false, and can always be 0. There is one implication clause per literal occurrence and no variable per occurrence.

2. For m≥1 compute $p=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m} y_j$ with m−1 binary XOR gates using the complete equivalences of [METHODS.md, Section 2.1](../../METHODS.md); for m=1 take p=y_1. Let H_0 and H_1 be the implication formula with even and odd marker parity, respectively. Neither formula includes the original long clauses.

3. For each original assignment x, let U(x) be the set of its unsatisfied clauses. The allowed marker sets are all T⊆U(x), and every such assignment has exactly one XOR-gate extension. Consequently $\#H_0-\#H_1=\sum_x\sum_{T\subseteq U(x)}(-1)^{|T|}=\#F$, since the inner sum is 1 exactly when U(x) is empty. A tautological clause forces its marker to zero, and repeated clauses cause no incorrect multiplicity after cancellation.

4. Each query has n original variables, m markers, and m−1 XOR outputs: N=n+2m−1. The ℓ implication clauses, four clauses per XOR, and final parity unit clause give M=O(ℓ+m) and width at most three. The explicit encoded bit length is O((n+m+ℓ) log(n+m+2)), polynomial in L under the stated explicit-input model.

5. Each parity count is at most 2^(n+m), because gate extensions are unique. The counts and their exact difference therefore require O(n+m) bits. Two sequential calls to the general fixed-width #SAT assumption, followed by exact subtraction, give A(n+m)L^{O(1)} time and polynomial space. The reported formalization profile gives its separately displayed weaker exponent.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- This is a two-query exact-counting reduction with subtraction, not a single parsimonious transformation. A SAT oracle that returns only YES or NO cannot supply the required counts.
- The measure is n+m, not n alone. The conclusion does not give a subexponential-in-n algorithm for arbitrary-width CNF with an unbounded number of clauses as a function of n.
- The clause count is controlled by literal occurrences ℓ, which need not be O(n+m). The primary claim therefore uses the general-density profile; no sparsification lemma or sparse-profile bound is assumed here.
- Unused declared variables remain in both formulas, so their powers-of-two contributions are retained. The result does not assume a compressed representation of exponentially many clauses or variables.
- The transformation is recorded as a catalog deduction without a novelty claim or a systematic latest-best comparison.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
